item.title: How to Alley Oop in NBA 2K27
item.description:
With the latest edition of the leading basketball franchise here, players will be eager to jump onto the court and learn how to alley-oop in NBA 2K27 , including how to throw the lob to a teammate, how to finish as the dunker, and how to perform self-alley-oops. This is one of the most satisfying plays to pull off in the sport, and aside from showing off, alley-oops are arguably the best options in 2 vs 1 breaks.

Xbox 1 1

NBA 2K27 Is Crossing Over With GTA 6

2K Sports premieres a new two-minute NBA 2K27 trailer teases a wide variety of content, including a collaboration with Grand Theft Auto 6.

By Dominik Bošnjak

How To Alley Oop In NBA 2K27

To throw the lob for an alley-oop, you'll ideally want to control a great passer, such as a Point Guard. You'll also need an open teammate to run toward the basket and finish the move.

  • Double tap [Y]

If you're controlling the entire team, you will then need to receive and dunk the ball by pressing [X] at the right time when the indicator appears .

This last bit won't be necessary if you're playing MyCareer and only have control of the passer.

How To Call For An Alley Oop

Without the ball and as a potential dunker, players can run toward the basket when open and use the following controls to call for an alley-oop.

  • Double tap [Y]

You will then need to press the button that appears above the player's head .

On easier difficulties, there is no button to press to finish an alley-oop. Meanwhile, for online matches, the button may be different each time to keep players on their toes.

Best Teams for Point Guards in MyCareer in NBA 2K27

The following modern and historic teams lack star guards, making them ideal for rising Point Guards in NBA 2K27's MyCareer.

By Joe Grantham

How To Self Alley Oop In NBA 2K27

Self alley-oops are best performed in 1-on-1 scenarios where the ball-handler has a height and physicality advantage , but ideally, they should be a good passer and, more importantly, athletic enough to pull off a dunk. They are also a great way to showboat on wide-open fast breaks , either in NBA games in front of the fans or at park games with friends and rivals.

Practice self alley-oops, other solo skills, and shooting in the Freeplay option under the Learn 2K tab.

Thankfully, the controls for self alley-oops are almost the same as they were in NBA 2K26 ​​​, but any players returning from more distant editions of the franchise will have to relearn.

  • Press [X] + [Y] at the same time while sprinting toward the basket .

This should lob the ball at the backboard, at which time a large indicator for [Y] will pop up.

  • Press [Y] at the right time for the perfect alley-oop dunk.

Mistiming this or pressing another button in haste will cause the alley-oop to fail , and defenders will likely have time to reclaim the loose ball.

NBA 2K27

item.title: Xbox Confirms Surprise Game Pass Addition for September 10
item.description:
Xbox Game Pass is getting a brand-new game in early September, with Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage scheduled to join the Microsoft subscription service. The game joins Xbox Game Pass as an enhanced remaster of Virtua Fighter 5 , which originally released in 2006.

Microsoft's premium subscription service offers a wide array of titles to choose from, spanning some of the console's biggest games. Many of the company's biggest first-party franchises are part of Xbox Game Pass, including new releases like Halo: Campaign Evolved and Forza Horizon 6 . The service includes a wealth of major releases from third-party developers as well, offering both AAA games like Game Freak's Beast of Reincarnation and popular indie games like Hollow Knight: Silksong . Now, Sega has surprised fans with the reveal of a popular fighting game coming to Xbox Game Pass.

Xbox Game Pass Adds Day-One Sequel to a Game With 5 TGA Nominations

The latest Xbox Game Pass release is a day-one follow-up to a widely praised title that lost the most high-profile 2022 GOTY award to Elden Ring.

By Dominik Bošnjak

Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage Is Coming to Xbox Game Pass

Sega recently confirmed that Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage will be coming to Xbox Game Pass on September 10. Sega confirmed in the newest Producer letter that the Virtua Fighter 5 remaster will be joining the Game Pass lineup, alongside its debut as part of Xbox on PC. Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage previously released on Xbox Series X/S and PS5 in October 2025 as the newest in a long line of Virtua Fighter 5 remasters, with a Nintendo Switch 2 version released later in March 2026.

Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage featured a wide variety of improvements to previous versions of the game. The new World Stage single-player mode serves as one of the main additions to the game, pitting players against a gauntlet of CPU-controlled fighters with playstyles based on Virtua Fighter 5 's top pros. World Stage also included cross-play support on all of its platforms, alongside the introduction of rollback netcode for the fighting game. Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage even received a nomination for Best Fighting Game at the 2025 Game Awards, though it would ultimately lose to Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves .

The newest version of Virtua Fighter 5 is the latest in a long line of remasters for the most recent entry in the iconic Virtua Fighter franchise. The original Virtua Fighter 5 first debuted in Japanese arcades in 2006, receiving multiple revisions before the first console version of the game launched on the PS3 in 2007. Sega has since launched multiple revisions and remasters for the game in the following years, including Final Showdown , Ultimate Showdown , and R.E.V.O. as the most recent major revision. World Stage first launched as a free update to Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O.

Xbox Game Pass Already Has 8 Games Confirmed for September 2026

Virtua Fighter 5 R.E.V.O. World Stage coming to Game Pass adds it to a select group of traditional fighting games on the service. Mortal Kombat 1 easily stands as one of the most well known, with the reboot of the Mortal Kombat franchise added to Game Pass in December 2025. Fans looking for a more lighthearted fighting game experience on the subscription service also have multiple options, with titles like Brawlhalla and Nickelodeon All-Stars Brawl 2 available.

item.title: One of 2026's Best Open-World Games Just Got Even Better (And It's Even On Sale)
item.description:
Crimson Desert wasn't everyone's cup of tea when it launched earlier this year, but then again, what game is? Pearl Abyss' ridiculously ambitious open-world game arrived with some undeniably rough edges, many of which I ran into myself when I reviewed it. Even then, though, I couldn't get over just how incredible its open world was. There were things about Crimson Desert that frustrated me, but every time I thought I had finally seen everything Pywel had to offer, I would wander off in another direction and find something that somehow made me fall in love with it all over again.

The game I reviewed back then also isn't really the game Crimson Desert is anymore. Pearl Abyss has spent the months since launch steadily addressing many of the problems players had with it, and now it has capped all of that off with the free Crimson Desert Enhanced update . The 2.0 update adds new story moments, changes progression in a pretty significant way, adds new skills, and makes several other improvements on top of everything Pearl Abyss has already done since March. Better yet, Crimson Desert is currently 20% off for the first time since launch, bringing its standard edition down from $69.99 to $55.99 on Steam and PS5, among other platforms, through September 9, 2026.

One Highly Anticipated Open-World RPG Is Getting Awfully Close to Be Skipping Gamescom 2026 ONL

Gamescom's Opening Night Live had plenty to offer, but the absence of one of gaming's most anticipated open-world RPGs is concerning.

By LB Beistad

Crimson Desert's Open World Was the Stuff of Dreams From the Beginning

Read GameRant's Review of Crimson Desert

  • Get Crimson Desert Enhanced on Steam
  • Get Crimson Desert Enhanced on Xbox
  • Get Crimson Desert Enhanced on PS5

When I called Crimson Desert 's open world the best I had ever seen in a game in my review, I knew exactly how ridiculous that probably sounded. I have spent years putting Breath of the Wild on a pedestal for the way it encourages curiosity, and Elden Ring is still one of the best examples I can think of when it comes to making an open world feel like it was actually designed to be explored rather than simply cleared. Somehow, though, Crimson Desert managed to take a lot of what I love about those games and then pile an almost unreasonable amount of interactivity on top of it, to the point where Pywel often felt closer to an actual place than a giant video game map.

—

More Games

One of the things I said in my review was that Crimson Desert operates by the rule of "If you think you can do it, you probably can," and that's still probably the easiest way I can describe what makes its open world so special. I could set out intending to complete a quest and somehow end up hunting wildlife for crafting materials, helping someone I stumbled across on the road, or poking around a cave because I thought there might be something hiding inside it. Then I'd get back to camp and spend who knows how long messing around there instead, because even the Greymanes' home eventually becomes its own little game within the game once you've built it up enough.

But I think the biggest reason Pywel worked so well for me was the way Crimson Desert handled its map. Rather than giving me a screen covered in icons and essentially telling me where all the interesting stuff was before I had even seen it, the game generally expected me to find things on my own first. That meant I was paying attention to the world around me rather than constantly opening the map to figure out which marker I wanted to chase next, and because there was almost always something waiting somewhere in the distance, I rarely felt like wandering off course was wasting my time. Sometimes I'd find an Abyss Artifact, while other times I'd stumble into a puzzle or some completely unexpected event, but the important part was that I usually found those things because I wanted to see what was there.

When I called Crimson Desert 's open world the best I had ever seen in a game in my review, I knew exactly how ridiculous that probably sounded.

At launch, the frustrating part was that some of Crimson Desert 's other systems could make getting back to that exploration more difficult than I wanted it to be. Inventory restrictions were probably one of the easiest examples, especially in a game that constantly gave me things I wanted to keep, and the progression system could make experimenting with new gear or investing in Damiane and Oongka feel like a much bigger commitment than it needed to be. I also ran into plenty of smaller quality-of-life frustrations along the way, and by the time I finished my review, I was basically hoping Pearl Abyss would eventually start shaving some of that friction away. As it turns out, I didn't have to wait very long.

Crimson Desert Has Barely Stopped Improving Since Launch

Pearl Abyss started making major changes to Crimson Desert almost immediately, with one of its first post-launch patches adding Private Storage and more Abyss Nexuses for fast travel before the game had even been out a week. By early April, that storage could be expanded to as many as 1,000 slots, and another update later that month added difficulty settings while improving the inventory and introducing even more storage options. Controller remapping eventually arrived in May, cross-save followed in July, and Pearl Abyss continued slipping in new skills, pets, mounts, housing improvements, mini-games, and other additions in between.

For context, Crimson Desert only launched in March 2026, meaning Pearl Abyss managed all of this in just over five months.

In fact, before Enhanced was even released, Pearl Abyss had already pushed out 17 patches containing more than 20 new features and content additions, along with more than 120 new mounts and pets and over 70 new outfits, equipment pieces, and items. I don't really care about the numbers themselves as much as what they represent here, because a lot of the changes weren't random additions meant to pad out an already gigantic game. Several of them directly addressed things players had been complaining about since launch, which is a big reason why the Crimson Desert I would recommend today isn't really the same one I reviewed in March.

Crimson Desert Enhanced Update Key Features

  • IMPROVED MAIN STORY – Adds new story scenes, dialogue, items, and Memory Fragments.
  • NEW ABYSS LINK SYSTEM – Makes progression between all three characters far less restrictive.
  • INDIVIDUAL SKILL RESETS – Lets each playable character reset their progression separately.
  • EIGHT NEW KLIFF SKILLS – Adds eight abilities unlocked through main story progression.
  • NEW GAME CARRYOVER – Carries Abyss Links and select currency into another playthrough.
  • NEW FLYING MOUNT CONTROLS – Adds camera-based and manual options for flying mounts.
  • EXPANDED LANGUAGE SUPPORT – Adds five voice languages and Arabic text support.

The Abyss Link system is probably the change I'm most interested in, because it directly addresses one of the things that bothered me most about progression when I reviewed the game. Previously, Abyss Artifacts were already incredibly valuable for Kliff, so spending resources on Damiane or Oongka could be difficult to justify when I knew I was going to spend most of my time playing as him anyway. With Enhanced, spending Abyss Artifacts to learn a skill on one character now gives the other playable characters an equivalent number of Abyss Links that can be used to learn their own skills, which means investing in Kliff no longer leaves everyone else quite so far behind.

I'm also curious to see just how much of a difference the story improvements make, because Crimson Desert 's main narrative was easily one of the areas where its open world basically outshined everything around it. I found Kliff to be fairly one-dimensional in the original version of the game, and it didn't help that I could spend so much time wandering around Pywel between main quests that I'd sometimes return to the story having almost completely lost track of what was happening. Enhanced added new scenes and conversations while also using things like knowledge entries, items, and Memory Fragments to give its bosses more narrative context, so Pearl Abyss clearly hasn't been afraid to go back and revisit an area of the game that could have easily been left alone after launch.

Before Enhanced was even released, Pearl Abyss had already pushed out 17 patches containing more than 20 new features and content additions, along with more than 120 new mounts and pets and over 70 new outfits, equipment pieces, and items.

More than anything, though, I think I'm impressed by how quickly Crimson Desert has managed to become a better version of itself this year. I already loved exploring Pywel when the game launched, even when some of the systems surrounding that exploration were getting on my nerves, and most of the complaints I had back then have either been addressed outright or at least improved considerably since. Enhanced feels like a continuation of that rather than some desperate attempt to bring players back, and if Pearl Abyss keeps treating Crimson Desert this way, I have a feeling Pywel is going to keep giving me reasons to return for a very long time.

Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons Is Treating Magic the Way More Open-World RPGs Should
Fable Has a Smart Fix for a Massive Open-World RPG Story Problem
1666: Amsterdam Turns Something Open-World Games Treat Like Scenery Into a Core Mechanic

For anyone who skipped Crimson Desert at launch, though, I'm not sure there has been a better time to finally give it a chance. The open world that sold me on the game in the first place is still there, but now there's far less standing between you and everything that made it so special to begin with. Throw in the Enhanced update and the game's first-ever 20% discount, and Pywel is looking better than it ever has.

Previously, Abyss Artifacts were already incredibly valuable for Kliff, so spending resources on Damiane or Oongka could be difficult to justify when I knew I was going to spend most of my time playing as him anyway. With Enhanced, spending Abyss Artifacts to learn a skill on one character now gives the other playable characters an equivalent number of Abyss Links that can be used to learn their own skills, which means investing in Kliff no longer leaves everyone else quite so far behind.

I'm also curious to see just how much of a difference the story improvements make, because Crimson Desert 's main narrative was easily one of the areas where its open world basically outshined everything around it. I found Kliff to be fairly one-dimensional in the original version of the game, and it didn't help that I could spend so much time wandering around Pywel between main quests that I'd sometimes return to the story having almost completely lost track of what was happening. Enhanced added new scenes and conversations while also using things like knowledge entries, items, and Memory Fragments to give its bosses more narrative context, so Pearl Abyss clearly hasn't been afraid to go back and revisit an area of the game that could have easily been left alone after launch.

Before Enhanced was even released, Pearl Abyss had already pushed out 17 patches containing more than 20 new features and content additions, along with more than 120 new mounts and pets and over 70 new outfits, equipment pieces, and items.

More than anything, though, I think I'm impressed by how quickly Crimson Desert has managed to become a better version of itself this year. I already loved exploring Pywel when the game launched, even when some of the systems surrounding that exploration were getting on my nerves, and most of the complaints I had back then have either been addressed outright or at least improved considerably since. Enhanced feels like a continuation of that rather than some desperate attempt to bring players back, and if Pearl Abyss keeps treating Crimson Desert this way, I have a feeling Pywel is going to keep giving me reasons to return for a very long time.

Warlock: Dungeons & Dragons Is Treating Magic the Way More Open-World RPGs Should
Fable Has a Smart Fix for a Massive Open-World RPG Story Problem
1666: Amsterdam Turns Something Open-World Games Treat Like Scenery Into a Core Mechanic

For anyone who skipped Crimson Desert at launch, though, I'm not sure there has been a better time to finally give it a chance. The open world that sold me on the game in the first place is still there, but now there's far less standing between you and everything that made it so special to begin with. Throw in the Enhanced update and the game's first-ever 20% discount, and Pywel is looking better than it ever has.

item.title: Once Human Season Reset: What Carries Over?
item.description:
If you are returning to Once Human or are a new player, you might be wondering what the status of Seasonal Resets, how scenario wipes are handled, and above all else, how character progression works after a Scenario ends.

If you are a bit confused or need help understanding everything related to how to preserve your items, seasonal rewards, and everything else you've unlocked with your hours invested in Once Human, then you've come to the right place. This guide will explain what you need to do when a reset happens, and how you need to handle previous seasonal content.

When Does the COD Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta End?

The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta has begun, but how long do you have left to play it? Here are the end times for the MW4 Open Beta.

By Nathan Round

How Do Seasonal Resets Work in Once Human

Once Human is a game in constant change, evolving through Scenarios, which are basically independent sandbox maps that pop up every season. Each of them have their own rules: Some are PvP-only focused, others are hardcore PvE experiences, or, like the new Deviation: Survive, Capture, Preserve scenario, with special rules similar to a monster-catcher game.

Now, every season, there are various things that are reset:

  1. Your character level goes back to 1.
  2. You lose your progress, quests, and Link Energy.
  3. All materials and items not deposited in the Seasonal Backpack or the Spacetime Backpack at the time of switching scenarios/Server wide wipe will be lost.
  4. You transfer the items, weapons, and blueprints you want transferred to your Spacetime Backpack; that way you can preserve them from being wiped. Some special items like Stellar Planula, Chrysalis Tokens, Scenario Exit Cards, Mitsuko Marks, and Colorful Badges won't disappear. These are considered account-wide items.
  5. At the end of the season, the rest of the regular items (Like Blueprints) won't simply disappear, but will be transferred to this Spacetime Backpack, which acts as a temporary inventory. You will have 30 days to move them to a new character in a new Scenario , or they will be transferred automatically to Eternaland and converted to Astral Sand.

Besides that, all of their cosmetic and scenario-exclusive special items obtained before they start a new scenario will remain . That also includes purchased content through the various stores in the game, and Season Pass Rewards qualified as Special Items / Gifts .

All of the considered cross-character rewards will always remain available, but be careful: Some items expire when opened (special consumables, for example) at the end of the season.

Scenario Reset & New Seasonal Content

If you are wondering what happens when a Scenario Resets at the end of the season, let's take a look at the whole process step by step. First, past scenarios can be played indefinitely as long as players remain inside said scenario and do not wish to start any other scenario whatsoever. The moment they change scenarios when a new season arrives, they will be offered the option to transfer certain items (the ones mentioned earlier), plus their characters will be reset to level 1 .

Unclaimed Seasonal Rewards (ex, unopened chests and unused currency) will remain in the Spacetime Backpack for 30 days ., until you create a new character, or, past that deadline, they will be transferred to Eternaland and turned into Astral Sand .

Now, Scenario servers do reset when they reach their final phase (that's often phase 6) , so players who want to still play the same scenario will be required to move ot a special off-season version or Permanent Scenario .

Players are then forced to move to the new scenario servers to keep playing the new content, or to transfer their items to Eternaland while keeping some to play in a Permanent Scenario.

It's up to each player's choice, but ultimately, if they want to keep up to date with the new content, and complete seasonal missions to earn Season Pass rewards, they need to play the latest scenario and its content.

item.title: When Does the COD Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta End?
item.description:
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 's Open Beta has officially kicked off, letting players jump into even more Multiplayer maps and modes, progress all the way to Level 30 to try out new weapons, and drop into the Zodiac Resurgence Map for Warzone . While the Modern Warfare 4 Beta has opened its doors for everyone, players can only play for a limited time. Here's how long you have left to enjoy the Beta.

Best Weapons in the COD Modern Warfare 4 Beta (Meta Weapon Tier List)

Playing the Early Access Beta or jumping in the following weekend for the Open Beta? here is a Meta Tier List ranking every gun in Modern Warfare 4.

By Nathan Round

When Does the COD Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta End?

COD Modern Warfare 4 Beta End Times

The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta ends on Tuesday, September 1 at 10 AM PT / 5 PM UTC. This gives players four total days to jump into the Open Beta before it closes for good. For those unsure of when the Beta ends, here is a rundown of all the end times by region:

Region

Open Beta End Times

Los Angeles (United States)

10:00 AM PT, September 1

Chicago (United States)

12:00 PM CT, September 1

New York (United States)

1:00 PM ET, September 1

Brasília (Brazil)

2:00 PM BRT, September 1

London (United Kingdom)

6:00 PM BST, September 1

Paris (France)

7:00 PM CEST, September 1

Johannesburg (South Africa)

7:00 PM SAST, September 1

Dubai (United Arab Emirates)

9:00 PM GST, September 1

Seoul (South Korea)

2:00 AM KST, September 2

Tokyo (Japan)

2:00 AM JST, September 2

Sydney (Australia)

3:00 AM AEST, September 2

Will There Be Another COD Modern Warfare 4 Beta?

When Can You Play Modern Warfare 4 Again?

As of the time of writing, Infinity Ward and Activision have revealed no details on another Beta weekend. With that being the case, there will not be another Beta period following the end of the Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta.

The next time you will be able to play Modern Warfare 4 is when its Campaign releases into Early Access on October 16 for those that pre-ordered the game , and then all other modes once the full game releases on Friday, October 23, 2026. Right now, all progress made during the Beta is exclusive to the Beta itself and will not carry over to the full release of the game.
